extracted.intended_audience: organizations preparing sustainability/ESG reports; sustainability reporting professionals, auditors, and policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for preparing sustainability (ESG/CSR) reports using the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) framework, including procedural requirements, disclosure topics, and quality criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modular structure of the GRI Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The GRI Standards have a modular structure comprising three series of Standards to support the reporting process: Universal Standards, Sector Standards, and Topic Standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modularity makes the standards easier to update and adapt; reporters should select the applicable combination of Universal, Sector and Topic Standards for their organization and impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: GRI Universal Standards (apply to all organizations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The GRI Universal Standards apply to all organizations and cover core sustainability issues related to a company’s impact on the economy, society, and the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Universal Standards as the base for any GRI-based report to ensure coverage of core impacts regardless of sector or size.

rubrics_metrics.name: GRI Sector Standards (sector-specific disclosures)
rubrics_metrics.description: The GRI Sector Standards apply to specific sectors, particularly those with the highest environmental impact, such as oil and gas, coal, and agriculture, aquaculture and fishing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations in high-impact sectors should apply relevant Sector Standards to ensure sector-specific impacts are reported consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: GRI Topic Standards (topic-specific disclosures)
rubrics_metrics.description: The GRI Topic Standards list disclosures relevant to a particular topic area (examples include Waste, Occupational Health and Safety, Biodiversity, Energy, Diversity and Equal Opportunity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select Topic Standards that match the organization’s material topics and include the listed disclosures to provide consistent, comparable data on those topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting review cycle (GSSB review every three years)
rubrics_metrics.description: GRI Standards and reporting criteria are reviewed every three years by the Global Sustainability Standards Board (GSSB), an independent body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report preparers should monitor updates on the three-year cycle to ensure reports follow the most recent Standards (e.g., revised Universal Standards published Oct 2021, effective Jan 2023).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to notify GRI (GRI 1: Foundation 2021 Req. 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Requirement 9 of GRI 1: Foundation 2021, notifying GRI of the use of the GRI standards is a mandatory step in reporting for associated organizations; registration via the GRI Standards Report Registration System is available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting organizations must notify/register when they use GRI Standards; responsibility for report quality and verification remains with the reporting organization and stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting in accordance vs in reference to GRI
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations may report either 'in accordance' with GRI (more stringent) or 'in reference' to GRI under the 2021 guidelines; both options involve notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'In accordance' requires meeting all applicable GRI requirements; choose the appropriate level and ensure notification and evidence of conformity where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enable third-party assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: The GRI standards aim to enable third parties to assess environmental impact from the activities of the company and its supply chain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports should present information in a clear, comparable manner and include sufficient data and methodology to allow independent assessment and verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of ESG metrics to disclose
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of ESG reporting include quantified measures of CO2 emissions, working and payment conditions, and financial transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include specific, quantifiable metrics (e.g., emissions in CO2-equivalent, workforce statistics) relevant to disclosed topics to improve comparability and usefulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with other international standards and principles
rubrics_metrics.description: GRI reporting standards were developed based on principles set in OECD Guidelines for Multinational Enterprises and UN Guiding Principles and were influenced by ISO 14010–14012, ISO 26000, OHSAS 18001, and ILO core conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters should consider alignment and cross-referencing with these established standards and conventions when preparing disclosures to enhance credibility and interoperability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality approach and definitional clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: There are differing approaches to materiality—GRI focuses on impact materiality, while other frameworks like SASB and ESRS may emphasize financial or double materiality; this can cause confusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state the materiality determination process used (impact, financial, or double materiality) and explain its implications for included disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double materiality requirement (EU/ESRS context)
rubrics_metrics.description: Double materiality requires public reporting of both sustainability factors affecting the company's financial materiality and its outward materiality (how the company affects society and the environment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations subject to ESRS/CSRD should address both inward (financial) and outward (impact) materiality in reports and reconcile any differences with GRI’s impact-focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent assurance of reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent assurance of sustainability reports may be demanded by stakeholders, and third-party assurance is standard practice for many large and mid-cap companies; absence of assurance is associated with lower quality and credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider obtaining external assurance to increase credibility; weigh cost against stakeholder expectations and risk of greenwashing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk of selective disclosure and greenwashing
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance with GRI is voluntary; outcomes depend on the quality and type of information reported, and firms may selectively disclose sustainability information which can enable greenwashing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure transparency and completeness, disclose limitations and methodologies, and be prepared for stakeholder scrutiny to mitigate selective reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder engagement and communication practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Good sustainability reporting practices include stakeholder relation mechanisms and communication strategies that encourage conjoint two-way sense making and sense giving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage stakeholders in defining material topics and in reviewing reports; use communications that enable dialogue rather than one-way messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality criteria for sustainability reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Research highlights requirements of comparability, transparency and reflection of sustainability performance as core aspects of report quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design reports to maximize comparability (consistent metrics/definitions), transparency (clear methods and limitations), and faithful reflection of performance (avoid selective presentation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and effective dates for Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised Universal Standards were published in October 2021 and came into effect for reporting in January 2023.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report preparers must apply the version of the Standards that is effective for the reporting period and be aware of transition provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report registration and public accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: GRI discontinued its publicly accessible sustainability disclosure database in 2021 but maintains a Report Registration System; notifying GRI is required for associated organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register reports when required and maintain public accessibility on company channels even if GRI's central database is not publicly maintained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity, resources and training for reporting quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Research suggests resources for sustainability reporting may be insufficient and staff undertrained in many companies; GRI provides training to address this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in staff training and resources, use available GRI training and guidance, and ensure data collection systems are adequate for robust reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interoperability and alignment with other reporting systems
rubrics_metrics.description: GRI has worked to achieve interoperability between GRI Standards and other systems such as ESRS and alignment efforts with the ISSB to reconcile multi-stakeholder and investor-focused reporting needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing reports, explicitly map GRI disclosures to other standards (ESRS, ISSB, SASB) where relevant to facilitate comparability and regulatory compliance.
